description: How information flows through a health system and how software supports it: the building blocks of health systems, district health information systems such as DHIS2, facility workflows from registration to claims, indicators and routine reporting, data quality, evaluation of information systems and the history and governance of health information systems in Africa. Taught through case-based simulations of a district health directorate, with realistic reporting cycles, dashboards and data quality reviews built in browser-based tools.
modelledOn: WHO, Framework and Standards for Country Health Information Systems (Health Metrics Network)
WHO, Data Quality Review: A Toolkit for Facility Data Quality Assessment
Wager, Lee and Glaser, Health Care Information Systems: A Practical Approach for Health Care Management
Braa and Sahay, Integrated Health Information Architecture: Power to the Users
outcomes: Describe the building blocks of a health system and map the information needs of patients, clinicians, managers and policy makers at each level.
Configure a district health information system with organisation units, data elements, data sets and indicators and use it to collect and aggregate routine data.
Model health facility workflows from registration to discharge and insurance claims and identify where information is created, used and lost.
Define, calculate and interpret health indicators and produce reports and dashboards that support decisions at facility, district and national level.
Assess routine data for completeness, timeliness and consistency, and design interventions that improve data quality and use.
Evaluate a health information system against its goals using established frameworks and propose improvements suited to African health systems.

units.title: Health systems and their information needs
topics: The WHO health system building blocks; health information as one of six; universal health coverage
Levels of care in Ghana: CHPS compounds, health centres, district, regional and teaching hospitals; the Ghana Health Service
Who needs what information: patients, clinicians, facility managers, district and regional directorates, ministries, donors
Data, information, knowledge and decisions; the information cycle from collection to action
Sources of health data: routine facility data, surveys (DHS, MICS), censuses, civil registration and vital statistics, surveillance

units.title: Health information system architecture
topics: Components of a national HIS: patient-level systems, aggregate systems, registries, logistics, HR and finance systems
Paper registers, tally sheets and summary forms and how they become electronic data
Fragmentation and vertical programme systems; the case for integration and enterprise architecture
Digital health building blocks and the OpenHIE architecture in outline
Open-source platforms in common use: DHIS2, OpenMRS, OpenLMIS, iHRIS

units.title: District health information systems
topics: DHIS2 concepts: organisation unit hierarchy, data elements, category combinations, data sets, periods
Aggregate versus individual (tracker) data; programme stages and events
Data entry, offline capture on Android and synchronisation over weak networks
Aggregation, disaggregation by age and sex, and analytics tables
Configuring a district instance with facilities, monthly reports and validation rules
Ghana's national rollout of DHIS2 and lessons from other African countries

units.title: Health facility workflows
topics: Patient journeys through an outpatient department: registration, triage, consultation, laboratory, pharmacy, billing
Inpatient admission, ward management, transfer, discharge and referral between levels of care
Maternal and child health clinics, immunisation sessions and outreach by community health nurses
Health insurance workflows: NHIS membership verification, claims preparation and submission, claims auditing in Ghana
Supply chain and pharmacy stock management; stock-outs and logistics reports
Workflow modelling with BPMN and swimlane diagrams; finding duplicated recording and delays

units.title: Indicators and reporting
topics: Indicator design: numerators, denominators, targets; input, process, output, outcome and impact indicators
Population denominators and catchment areas; coverage rates for antenatal care, skilled delivery and immunisation
Programme indicators for malaria, HIV, TB and maternal health; national and SDG indicator frameworks
Reporting cycles, deadlines and feedback to facilities; avoiding reporting for its own sake
Dashboards, pivot tables, maps and scorecards for district management meetings
From data to decisions: district league tables and performance reviews

units.title: Data quality in health
topics: Dimensions of data quality: completeness, timeliness, accuracy, consistency, validity
Validation rules, outlier detection and internal consistency checks between related data elements
Data quality audits and verification: re-counting registers against reported figures; verification factors
Root causes of poor data: workload, training, form design, incentives, supervision
Improving data use: data review meetings, feedback, a culture of information use (PRISM framework)
Running a data quality review on a simulated district's monthly reports

units.title: Evaluating health information systems
topics: Why systems fail: design-reality gaps, sustainability, pilots that never scale
Evaluation frameworks: HMN assessment, PRISM, the DeLone and McLean success model
Measuring usability, adoption, data use and impact on health outcomes
Costing a health information system: total cost of ownership and sustainability planning

units.title: Health information systems in Africa
topics: History of HIS in Africa: from paper registers to DHIS2 and national digital health strategies
Governance, ownership and donor coordination; the role of ministries and health services
Infrastructure realities: power, connectivity, devices, local support and hosting
Ghana's digital health initiatives: Lightwave e-Health, the national health insurance claims system, e-Tracker
Privacy and data protection under Ghana's Data Protection Act 843 for health data

units.title: Project
topics: Assessing the information needs of a chosen district or facility
Designing data sets, indicators and dashboards to meet those needs
Planning data quality checks and a feedback cycle
Project: a configured district reporting system with a written evaluation and improvement plan

schedule.title: Health information as a building block
schedule.exercise: Pick one Ghana Health Service level of care and list, for one week, every piece of information its staff produce and every decision that information supports.

tasks.title: Match five health information needs (patient, clinician, district director, ministry) to the report or system that should serve each, scored on fit
Decide which data source (routine facility data, a survey, civil registration) best answers four stated health questions, with reasons
Trace one piece of clinic data from collection to a district decision, naming the step where it could be delayed or lost, and propose a fix

schedule.title: Components of a national health information system
schedule.exercise: Draw a diagram of how a paper tally sheet becomes an electronic district report, labelling every hand-off and where errors can enter.

tasks.title: Draw a BPMN or flow diagram of a paper register being tallied, summarised and entered into a computer, marking each point data can be miscopied
Decide, for a district running five separate vertical-programme systems, which to integrate first and justify the order
Compare DHIS2, OpenMRS, OpenLMIS and iHRIS for a district's needs and recommend which to deploy first, with a reason for each remaining gap

schedule.title: DHIS2 concepts
schedule.exercise: Explain the difference between aggregate and tracker data in DHIS2 with one example of each for a maternal health programme.

tasks.title: Design an organisation unit hierarchy and a data set with data elements for a district's monthly immunisation report
Decide whether five indicators (bed count, individual patient visit, monthly stock count, birth record) need aggregate or tracker capture, with reasons
Capture a week of outreach immunisation data offline on a simulated Android device and walk through what happens when it synchronises over a weak network

schedule.title: Aggregation and district configuration
schedule.exercise: Design the validation rules you would add to a district data set to catch an impossible monthly figure before it is submitted.

tasks.title: Configure a district instance with three facilities, a monthly reporting data set and two validation rules, then test them against a bad submission
Disaggregate a year of facility visit counts by age and sex and compute the share each group contributes to the district total
Compare Ghana's DHIS2 rollout approach with one other African country's and recommend one lesson a new district adoption should apply

schedule.title: Patient journeys and workflows
schedule.exercise: Map the steps a patient follows from registration to discharge at an outpatient department, marking where waiting time is longest.

tasks.title: Draw a swimlane diagram of an outpatient visit from registration through triage, consultation, laboratory, pharmacy and billing
Model the workflow of a community outreach immunisation session as a BPMN diagram, including the community health nurse's steps
Map an inpatient admission, ward stay, transfer and discharge pathway and mark two steps where a referral could be lost between levels of care

schedule.title: Insurance claims and supply workflows
schedule.exercise: Explain the steps of an NHIS claim from treatment to payment and identify where a data entry error would cause a rejection.

tasks.title: Walk a simulated outpatient visit through NHIS membership verification and claims preparation, and decide how to handle a lapsed membership
Track a month of pharmacy stock movements, detect an impending stock-out and decide what order quantity would avoid it
Redraw a workflow that currently records the same vital signs twice, removing the duplication while keeping every needed record point

schedule.title: Indicator design
schedule.exercise: Write a numerator, denominator, target and data source for three programme indicators of your choice, and state what an increase would mean for policy.

tasks.title: Write the numerator, denominator and target for an outcome indicator and an output indicator from a given programme goal, and justify the choice
Compute a coverage rate for skilled delivery from catchment population and facility delivery counts, and flag if the denominator looks wrong
Choose three indicators from a national framework that best track a malaria programme's progress and justify dropping two candidates

schedule.title: Reporting cycles and data use
schedule.exercise: Design a one-page scorecard for a district management meeting that compares facilities on three indicators and flags the two needing attention.

tasks.title: Build a district league table from monthly indicator data and decide which two facilities most need a supervisory visit, with evidence
Redesign a reporting calendar that currently causes facilities to miss two deadlines a quarter, and justify the new deadlines and feedback loop
Chair a simulated district review meeting that turns a league table into three agreed actions, scored on how well data supported each decision

schedule.title: Data quality
schedule.exercise: Explain the five dimensions of data quality with one concrete health-reporting example of each dimension failing.

tasks.title: Classify ten data problems found in a district's monthly report under the correct data quality dimension
Write two validation and consistency rules that would have caught a reported figure that contradicts a related data element
Audit a facility's monthly report against its register by re-counting a sample, and compute the verification factor

schedule.title: Causes and culture of data quality
schedule.exercise: Write a short root-cause analysis for a facility that consistently under-reports, considering workload, training, forms, incentives and supervision.

tasks.title: Diagnose the root cause of a facility's repeated reporting errors from five clues (workload, form design, training, supervision, incentives)
Design a data review meeting agenda using the PRISM framework that turns a facility's recurring errors into a feedback and improvement plan
Run a data quality review on a simulated district's monthly reports, find the root causes behind three flagged figures and propose fixes

schedule.title: Why systems fail and evaluation
schedule.exercise: Pick one real class of digital health failure (design-reality gap, pilot that never scaled, unsustainable funding) and explain how you would have avoided it.

tasks.title: Diagnose which design-reality gap caused a described pilot health system to fail, and propose the single change most likely to have saved it
Apply the DeLone and McLean success model to rate a described system on its information quality, use and net benefits, with evidence for each score
Estimate the total cost of ownership of a district health information system over five years and flag the year sustainability funding runs short

schedule.title: Governance and infrastructure realities
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page case for who should own and fund a district health information system, weighing ministry, donor and facility roles.

tasks.title: Decide which actor (ministry, donor, district, facility) should own three disputed decisions about a shared health information system, with reasons
Plan how a facility with unreliable power and connectivity should capture and later submit its monthly report, choosing offline-capable steps
Review a scenario for a breach of health data and decide the notification and remediation steps required under Ghana's Data Protection Act 843

schedule.title: District reporting capstone
schedule.exercise: Assess the information needs of a chosen district, then write a one-page evaluation of your finished reporting system against the DeLone and McLean dimensions, naming its biggest remaining weakness.

tasks.title: Assess the information needs of a chosen district from a short scenario and list the three most urgent gaps, with reasons
Design two data sets, three indicators and a dashboard view that address the district's needs, and diagram the data flow from facility to ministry

Configure a district reporting system project with organisation units, data sets and validation rules, write an evaluation against a success model, and an improvement plan, scored on a capstone rubric
